<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **22** documentable anchor(s).

**6** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-driven.mdx`  _(via ObjectSchemaBase (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/objects.mdx`  _(via chainField (symbol, a field of class ObjectCheck; a field of interface SealPlan), chainField (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line; a string literal in refuseUnknownSealChainField), tenant_id (literal, a string literal in AUDIT_SEAL_DEFAULT_CHAIN_FIELD; a string literal in plans))_
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via tenant_id (literal, a string literal in AUDIT_SEAL_DEFAULT_CHAIN_FIELD; a string literal in plans))_
- `content/docs/deployment/seed-tenancy-repair.mdx`  _(via tenant_id (literal, a string literal in AUDIT_SEAL_DEFAULT_CHAIN_FIELD; a string literal in plans))_
- `content/docs/permissions/record-view-auditing.mdx`  _(via tenant_id (literal, a string literal in AUDIT_SEAL_DEFAULT_CHAIN_FIELD; a string literal in plans))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/config-resolution.mdx`  _(via tenant_id (literal, a string literal in AUDIT_SEAL_DEFAULT_CHAIN_FIELD; a string literal in plans))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/implementation-status.mdx`  _(via tenant_id (literal, a string literal in AUDIT_SEAL_DEFAULT_CHAIN_FIELD; a string literal in plans))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via tenant_id (literal, a string literal in AUDIT_SEAL_DEFAULT_CHAIN_FIELD; a string literal in plans))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via tenant_id (literal, a string literal in AUDIT_SEAL_DEFAULT_CHAIN_FIELD; a string literal in plans))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `created_at (literal, 46 pages)`
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **176** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 162fe54fbbd14d3415a4d72e13abd9a610eedcaf` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8637a2423eb508323fe6849a1f3eb05449a69861` — the merge of head `a93c0509bbc92047d9a21b92287fa4fc2c4ce130` into base `162fe54fbbd14d3415a4d72e13abd9a610eedcaf`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8637a2423eb508323fe6849a1f3eb05449a69861 && git checkout 8637a2423eb508323fe6849a1f3eb05449a69861
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 162fe54fbbd14d3415a4d72e13abd9a610eedcaf a93c0509bbc92047d9a21b92287fa4fc2c4ce130 && git checkout -B drift-repro 162fe54fbbd14d3415a4d72e13abd9a610eedcaf && git merge --no-ff a93c0509bbc92047d9a21b92287fa4fc2c4ce130

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 162fe54fbbd14d3415a4d72e13abd9a610eedcaf
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 162fe54fbbd14d3415a4d72e13abd9a610eedcaf` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

L1 thread L1-a for area o1-A, on the final head declared in 6913980937. Read: card #34164, the PR body, and the full diff against merge base `951eceee` (12 files, +750/−19), round 1 and round 2 (`d919486f..ebd7fbd7`: the changeset and `objects.mdx` only) alike. The L2 record at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` is review#1's and is not repeated here.

- **Card relation.** `Fixes #34164`; no closing keyword sits next to any other number (#34352, #33773, #33675 and #34220 are named without one). The card's done condition is pinned on a real kernel and through the real command. `audit-seal-chain-field-34164.test.ts` seals one chain per organization for an object whose `organization_id` is registry-injected (the test asserts it is not declared). `verify.chain-field-34164.integration.test.ts` spawns `os audit verify --org org_x --json` and gets org_x's chain only, `modified` after a database-level edit, and `--org org_y` still clean.
- **One reader.** `chainValueOf` / `sealChainFieldOf` (`audit-seal/canonical.ts`) replace both `tenantOf` copies. I counted the sealer's five chain reads (window, late, page, leaf filter, plus the plan's column check) and the verifier's live-row read. All go through it, and no `row.tenant_id` read is left in `sealer.ts` or `verifier.ts`. The signed body keeps the member name `tenant_id`, so the bytes are unchanged. That is pinned by base-sealer digests (leaf, body, root) for both the default and an explicit `chainField: 'tenant_id'`, with an ablation that drops the column and turns both red.
- **Authoring refusal.** `refuseUnknownSealChainField` refuses only a NAMED column that is neither declared nor in `resolveInjectedSystemColumns(object)`, located at `lifecycle.seal.chainField`. The spec test covers an unknown name, an undeclared `tenant_id`, and `organization_id` under the three tenant opt-outs. The unnamed default case is not refused here: it stays the sealer's `error`, and its narrowing is #34352 (open). That is consistent with `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. The sealer's `hasOwnProperty(fields, chainField)` backstop is pinned for a definition that skipped the parse, with an ablation.
- **The import cycle** `object.zod.ts` ⇄ `injected-system-columns.ts` is function-only (called at parse time only), and the body records CJS and ESM loads of the built `@objectstack/spec/data` refusing `chainField: 'nope'`.
- **Docs sentences checked against the diff.**
  - `content/docs/data-modeling/objects.mdx` § Sealed audit objects: the `tenant_id` default; refusal of any name that is not declared or injected, with the three opt-outs; an object with neither column still parses and is reported; the platform-global case is reported; an empty chain value joins the no-organization rows (`chainValueOf` → `null` → deployment chain); `--org` reads the same column.
  - `content/docs/references/data/object.mdx`: regenerated from the new `.describe()`, which matches the refusal.
- **Changeset.** `minor` on `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/plugin-audit` (`Metadata-protocol: added`). The five bullets match the code, as above. `Skills-docs: follow-up #33773`: open, and its scope addition 6913220571 covers `lifecycle.md` § Sealing; `skills/**` is untouched. No `content/docs/releases/`.
- **Tier.** Tier H by `docs/adr/0154-*`: one appended note, no earlier sentence edited, as its status line says. +769 lines, under 3,000.
- **Checks on this head (check-runs, latest per name).** 68 names: 56 success, 12 skipped (path-filtered, opt-in and queue-only), 0 failed, 0 pending. Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check and Check Changeset are success.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ebd7fbd78affdb93461d489821ff39ba2e50bead`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts, docs/adr/0154-audit-ledger-tamper-evidence-sealer-signed-checkpoints-amendments-verify.md + packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/canonical.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/sealer.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/signed-body.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/verifier.ts
Security-touching: yes

Read: card #34164 with all six comments (claim 6906547049 and its seat ruling, takeover claim 6913075855, amendment 6913162434, dev reports 6911927317 and 6913929391), the PR body, the 12-file net diff against `origin/main`, the PR comments (hand-off 6912069272, final-head 6913980937, the L1 ACCEPT), and the check-runs on this head: 60 success, 12 skipped, 0 failed, with `Check Changeset`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core`, `Build Core` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` all success. Rule text read on main: AGENTS.md (Prime Directives 12 to 14, Post-Task step 3), ADR-0154 with its 2026-11-14 amendment, `injected-system-columns.ts`, `packages/spec/liveness/object.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`. Code outside the diff was read, not reviewed: `amendment-writer.ts`, `seed.ts`, `sys-audit-checkpoint.object.ts`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set, widened.** `lifecycle.seal` is a strict object, so `chainField` was refused as an unknown key on main and is accepted now as an optional string. One new refusal, `refuseUnknownSealChainField`, fires only when the key is present and names a field that is neither declared nor in `resolveInjectedSystemColumns(object).names`. Nothing that parsed on main is refused on this head. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is named right.
- **Default path unchanged.** A seal that names no `chainField` reaches the same plan (`sealChainFieldOf` answers `tenant_id`), the same sealer-time check (`hasOwnProperty(fields, 'tenant_id')`) and the same reader result as the two removed `tenantOf` copies. `plan.columns`, the signed body members and `checkpointSeedContext` are untouched, and the field name is not in the signed bytes, so a `tenant_id` object's leaf input, signed body and root are byte-identical. The base-sealer digests in `audit-seal-chain-field-34164.test.ts` pin this for the default and for `chainField: 'tenant_id'`.
- **Public surface.** `@objectstack/plugin-audit` gains three exports from `audit-seal/canonical.ts` (`AUDIT_SEAL_DEFAULT_CHAIN_FIELD`, `sealChainFieldOf`, `chainValueOf`); nothing is removed. The sealer's `error` report is reworded; it is a log line, not a contract.
- **Injected plan read with no deployment.** A `chainField: 'organization_id'` on an object its deployment declares platform-global passes authoring, and the sealer reports it at `error` and does not seal it. This is loud, and the docs page and changeset say so. Accepted as shipped.
- S1 (should-fix) — the accept-set for the new key is wider than its one reader honours.
  - `chainValueOf` answers a chain only for a non-empty string. A named column of a type that never yields one (number, boolean, date, json) parses, and every row then seals into the deployment chain with no refusal and no report. That is the outcome the helper's own docblock, and the sealer's S3 comment, say must not pass silently.
  - `id` is always in the injected names (even under `systemFields: false`), and `created_at` joins it with the audit family, so both pass as chain columns, though `valueFields` refuses both.
  - Refusing these for a NAMED column is free on this head and a `narrowed` change after release. The same collapse exists on main for a non-text `tenant_id`, so the default half belongs with #34352.
  - Fix here for the named case, or widen #34352's scope in writing before landing.

### ② Semver level

- `Metadata-protocol: added` takes at least `minor` on each package the diff moves (AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3). The changeset is `minor` on `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/plugin-audit`: correct. `@objectstack/cli` gains a test file only and needs none.
- Both declaration lines are line-initial in the PR body and in the changeset body, and they agree. `(widening)` matches ①; no BREAKING banner or ADR-0087 disposition is owed.
- Liveness and authorable-surface: both baselines govern `object.lifecycle` at the top-level key (`liveness/object.json` `lifecycle`, `authorable-surface/data.json` `data/Object:lifecycle`). Neither carries a row for the nested `seal.valueFields`, so none is owed for `seal.chainField`. The regenerated `content/docs/references/data/object.mdx` matches the new `.describe()`.
- `Skills-docs: follow-up #33773`: open, and its scope addition 6913220571 names the two `skills/**` files. `skills/**` is untouched.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Ruling "the authoring refusal replaces the sealer-time error" half done** (round-1 deviation and open question A/B): answered by the seat's 09:00Z ruling in hand-off 6912069272. The PR stays the widening, and the default-case refusal is #34352 (open, unclaimed). The retained sealer check is also the backstop for definitions that skip the parse. Agreed.
- **Changeset `minor` against the dispatch template's `patch`**: the dev is right, by the AGENTS.md rule quoted in ②.
- **Import cycle `object.zod.ts` and `injected-system-columns.ts`**: both crossing bindings (`resolveInjectedSystemColumns`, `isTenancyDisabled`) are function declarations called only inside a refinement at parse time. Accepted. `Build Core` and `Test Core` are green on this head.
- **Loose end: `chainField` also listed in `valueFields`**: not ruled and not carded. Answered as S2 below.
- **Loose end: platform-global deployment**: answered in ①, accepted as shipped.
- **Round-2 flags** (body written by the seat, gates derived for two paths, stale-tree warning, trailer form, the advisory `check-closing-target-claim` reading): process items for the seat. None changes the tree under review.
- **SQL push-down**: no new id materialisation and no new in-app join. `chainValueOf` replaces a same-shaped per-row read in loops that already page a window on `(created_at, id)`. Grouping rows by chain in the application predates this PR.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`** against the ruling and its first consumer.
- The key is optional, defaults to `tenant_id`, must name a field the object has, injected columns count, and a named unknown is refused with one located issue at `lifecycle.seal.chainField`. That is the ruling as narrowed at 09:00Z.
- First consumer (cloud#4128, `sys_ai_audit_log`, organization in injected `organization_id`, no `tenant_id`): `chainField: 'organization_id'` parses, and the registry-injected column satisfies the sealer's plan check. Holds.
- S2 (should-fix) — a `chainField` that is also a `valueFields` member is accepted. The column then enters the leaf as a commitment while its value travels in clear in the signed `tenant_id`, in `chain_key` and in the proof bundle. That is against D1's reason for commitments and D9's "a bundle holds no value". Refuse the overlap for a named column here, or record the default-column half on #34352.

**`docs/adr/0154-…md`** against its first consumer and its execution plan.
- The note is add-only. D4 does define the chain as an organization id, so keeping the member name `tenant_id` is sound. The D5 reading matches `chainValueOf` (an empty value joins the deployment chain). "One reader" matches the tree: no `row.tenant_id` read is left in `sealer.ts` or `verifier.ts`.
- The note's D10 bullet "The chain column is a clear column of the leaf … like every other declared column" is false for the overlap in S2. Its consequent (a moved row reads `modified`) holds either way, because the column is always in the leaf. Settle it with S2.
- S3 (should-fix) — the note and the docs page are silent on changing `chainField` on an object that already has checkpoints. Read from the code, not measured: where the old and new columns disagree, the sealer's window pass seals the last sealed window's rows again under the new chain key (reported as `listed_twice`), and a `--org` check reads earlier rows as `late`, unsealed. Both fail closed. State the rule (the chain column is fixed once an object has checkpoints, or what a change costs) in the note and in `objects.mdx`.
- S4 (should-fix) — the note's status cites claim 6906547049, whose ruling says the authoring refusal replaces the sealer-time error. The tree implements the later 09:00Z ruling instead. Cite hand-off 6912069272 and #34352, and add one sentence that an object with neither column still parses and is reported by the sealer.
- N1 (nit) — the 2026-11-14 amendment added a pointer in the status line and at D4. This note leaves D5, D10 and the "Names this record fixes" row (`{ valueFields: string[] }`) with no pointer to it.

**Implementing files.**
- `canonical.ts`: `chainValueOf` is the removed `tenantOf` with the column as a parameter; `sealChainFieldOf` answers the default for an absent key. Agrees with the contract.
- N2 (nit) — `sealChainFieldOf` also answers `tenant_id` for an empty or non-string `chainField` on a definition that skipped the parse, where a lacking column is reported instead.
- `sealer.ts`: the five chain reads (window accept, late accept, page grouping, the part's re-read filter, the plan check) all go through the plan's `chainField`. The plan check keeps reporting an object without its chain column at `error` and does not seal it. Agrees.
- `signed-body.ts`: comment only; the body shape is unchanged. Agrees.
- `verifier.ts`: the one live-row read (rows no checkpoint holds, and the bundle's `unsealed` entries) goes through `chainValueOf`. Held rows are judged from each checkpoint's signed `row_ids` and recorded column set, so checkpoints written before this change verify exactly as before. Agrees.
- N3 (nit) — `sys_audit_checkpoint.chain_key` is bounded at 259 for an organization id, and `tenant_id` is a lookup to `sys_organization`. A chain column that is not an organization id fits neither description. S1 settles what may be named.

**Attempts to break it.** None of these found a way to change a sealed row unseen.
- Verifying old checkpoints after the key lands.
- Two objects sharing a chain: every checkpoint read, the unique index and the seed coordinate carry `sealed_object`.
- A row moved between organizations: reads `modified` in its own chain.
- Whether the signed bytes include or omit the field name: omitted, and the default stays byte-identical.
- Changing `chainField` on a sealed object: covered by S3; it fails closed.

Implemented-by: `claude/area-A2-34164`
Reviewed-by: `session_01ASNY8Ywba8ySbMdWvra2vS`

**VERDICT: PASS**
